import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch.  Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# ChangeSpec name -> branch name conversion.
is_changespec = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_changespec:
        # ChangeSpec ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I’m using the `/sase_plan` skill to produce and submit the required implementation plan, plus `/sase_memory_read` because this bug is in an xprompt workflow. I’ll inspect the screenshot and relevant code/tests read-only, choose the plan tier, validate until clean, and run `sase plan propose` before touching any source files.

The screenshot confirms the defect is in the composed transcript: the `---` separator is followed by an extra blank line before `# New Query`. I’m tracing whether that whitespace originates in the built-in `#fork` template, prompt composition, or transcript rendering, and I’ll make the plan include a regression test at the narrowest stable boundary.

The raw launch artifact isolates the trigger: `#gh:… #fork:lt …` produced a literal leading space on the rendered heading, while the query body was normalized. The core fork envelope itself is clean, so I’m using `/sase_repo` now to inspect the linked GitHub workflow’s exact empty `prompt_part`; that composition boundary is the remaining difference between a clean reproduction and the captured failure.

The root cause is now pinned down: launch-deferred `#fork` expansion goes through `expand_embedded_workflows_in_query`, the one prompt-part expansion path that does not force a leading `%xprompts_enabled:false` marker onto its own line. With a preceding `#gh` reference, the marker remains inline (`#gh:… %xprompts_enabled:false`), so later stripping/Markdown formatting can transfer the separator space onto `# New Query`. I’m authoring this as a `tale`: one focused shared-invariant fix plus regression coverage is appropriate for a single coding agent.

The required first `--explain` pass found the current tale schema now requires `title` and `goal` in frontmatter in addition to `tier`. I’m applying those validator-mandated fields and will revalidate without `--explain`, as the skill requires.

The `tale` plan now validates with zero warnings. It scopes the fix to a shared disabled-marker line-boundary helper, wires all three expansion paths to the same invariant, and adds both focused and composed `#gh … #fork …` regression coverage. I’m submitting it now with `sase plan propose`; no source files have been changed.

n="{{ n }}"
if [ "$n" -lt 1 ]; then
  echo "ERROR: n must be >= 1 (got '$n')" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Ask Apollo for the nth most recent supported image (newest first). The
# globs and ~ are expanded by the remote shell; n is a validated integer.
basename=$(ssh apollo "cd ~/tmp/screenshots 2>/dev/null && ls -1t -- *.png 2>/dev/null | sed -n '${n}p'")
if [ -z "$basename" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: no screenshot #$n found on apollo (~/tmp/screenshots)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p ~/tmp/screenshots
if ! scp -pq "apollo:~/tmp/screenshots/$basename" ~/tmp/screenshots/"$basename" >&2; then
  echo "ERROR: failed to copy '$basename' from apollo" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "local_path=$HOME/tmp/screenshots/$basename"
